newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE OUT TO PLEASE HOME FANS.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE OUT TO PLEASE HOME FANS.

text.p: Nordic skiing star Bjorn Daehlie of Norway, who has already won everything he could dream of, goes for more in front of his adoring home fans in the world championships starting on Friday.

The 29-year-old, who had to be content with one gold medal in the relay at last year's world championships in Thunder Bay, Canada, said he looked forward to the 10-day festival in the port of Trondheim, currently celebrating its millennium.

"There will be lots of people expecting me do to well and I don't want to disappoint them," said Daehlie, the greatest cross-country skier of all time with six world titles, five Olympic golds and a record 35 World Cup wins.

Daehlie's most dangerous rival should once again be veteran Vladimir Smirnov. The 32-year-old from Kazakhstan, tired of finishing second to Daehlie, took a stylish revenge in Thunder Bay where he won three gold medals.
Hampered by a cold when this season started, Smirnov has fully recovered and proved it by winning a World Cup event last month in Lahti, Finland.
"I feel fine now," said Smirnov. "The Norwegians will be hard to beat but I'll do my best."

The ageing Smirnov said he was getting tired of the relentless training and might soon end his career. But a gold medal in Trondheim could persuade him to carry on until next year's Olympics in Nagano, Japan.

Finland, often outclassed by Norway in major competitions, have reasons to be ambitious this time as Mika Myllylae and Jari Isometsae keep showing on the World Cup circuit that they are no longer afraid of anyone.
But the nation most capable of challenging the mighty Norwegians seems to be Italy with not only Silvio Fauner, the reigning 50 km world champion, but also Fulvio Valbusa and Marco Albarello.
In the women's cross-country races, Russia will start hot favourite with Yelena Vialbe and Ljubov Yegorova both capable of winning almost every event.

World Cup holder Manuela di Centa of Italy would love to win her first world title but has been struggling to recapture her best form since she was injured in a fall last November. Italy will also look to in-form Stefania Belmondo, who scored five wins this winter.

Norway, hoping for a repeat of their memorable showing in the 1994 Lillehammer Olympics, could shine in the Nordic combined event, where holders Fred Boerre Lundberg and Knut Tore Apeland will be among the favourites alongside Kenji Ogiwara of Japan.
In the ski jumping, all eyes will be on new 17-year-old sensation Primoz Peterka of Slovenia, who burst into the limelight by winning the coveted Four Hills tournament last month.
Peterka, who leads the World Cup standings, will challenge Austrian Andreas Goldberger, Dieter Thoma of Germany and Takanobu Okabe of Japan.
Organisers, worried about allegations of blood-doping in the sport, said blood tests would be performed during the competition as well as urine tests.
Competition conditions should be ideal as fresh snow has fallen in the last few days and the weather forecast predicts relatively mild temperatures.
The championships open on Friday with the men's 30 km free style cross-country race and end on March 2 with the grand finale, the men's 50 km.
